name: ericw-tools 2.0.0-alpha7 (Quake II, experimental)
summary: Experimental: the qbsp, vis and light compilers in their Quake II mode, from a 2.x pre-release.
description:
This is the experimental Quake II toolchain, and it is a separate document from the stable Quake 1 one for a reason that is not organisational: they are different programs. “ericw-tools 0.18.1 (Quake 1)” describes release v0.18.1, the newest release upstream has not marked a pre-release. Quake II support lives in the 2.x line, and the whole of that line — up to and including this one — is published as a pre-release. Pinning a pre-release for Q1 would be a downgrade of a qualified path; not pinning one for Q2 would mean no Q2 path at all. So there are two documents, two versions and two sets of capability ids, and a Q1 pipeline can never resolve to this tool.

Everything below was measured by running 2.0.0-alpha7 on Linux against a synthetic Q2 map, not read across from the Q1 profile. Seven things differ, and each of them would have been a plausible-looking wrong answer:

1. The archive has no `bin/` directory and no root directory: `qbsp` is at the archive root. The v0.18.1 archive unpacks to `ericw-tools-v0.18.1-Linux/bin/qbsp`.
2. `maputil` is new; v0.18.1 has no such program.
3. The log files are named differently. v0.18.1 writes `vis.log` and `light.log`; this writes `<stem>.log`, `<stem>-vis.log` and `<stem>-light.log`.
4. qbsp writes a `<stem>.texinfo.json` beside the BSP, and `light` reads it back — `Loading extended texinfo flags from …`. It is therefore declared as an input to the lighting step and staged with the BSP, exactly as the portal file is for vis. A lighting job that did not stage it would succeed, silently, with the wrong surface flags.
5. `-lit` does nothing here. Asked for on a Quake II BSP it prints `.lit colored light output requested on command line.` and writes no file, because Quake II lightmaps are already RGB inside the BSP. There is no `lit` option in this document.
6. `bspinfo` **writes files** in 2.x — `<bsp>.json`, `<bsp>.geometry.obj` and one PNG per lightmap atlas — where v0.18.1 only printed a report. Its action therefore asks for write access to the workspace and declares those outputs.
7. Quake 1's special texture-name rules do not apply. In Quake II a brush's contents and surface flags come from the `.wal` the map references — or from a `.wal_json` beside it — which is why the base game data root is required rather than optional. A compile with nothing bound there still exits 0 and still writes a BSP; it just writes one where every surface has default flags, no playerclip and no sky. That is the worst kind of failure, so it is refused at the binding instead.

Three roots, bound separately, because they are three separate things a user has and can move independently: the executables (`tool_root`), the base game data (`game_root`, passed as `-basedir`, the directory that holds `textures/`), and the mod (`content_root`, passed as `-gamedir`). Compiling a plain `baseq2` map means binding the last two to the same directory, which is exactly what upstream's own auto-detection does when a map is compiled inside `baseq2/maps`.

`-nodefaultpaths` is deliberately not sent. It looks like the safe choice — confine the search to what the user bound — and it was measured to break texture lookup even with `-basedir` given explicitly. `-nocolor` is sent everywhere, so a captured log is text rather than escape codes.

acquisition.title: Use a copy you already have
acquisition.hint: choose the unpacked ericw-tools 2.x folder — the one with qbsp directly inside it, not inside bin/
acquisition.note: Download the 2.0.0-alpha7 pre-release for your platform from the ericw-tools homepage and unpack it, or use a newer alpha or your own build. You are the authority for what you pointed at, and a different alpha may behave differently from the one this document measured.

acquisition.title: Find them on PATH
acquisition.note: Whatever version is first on PATH — which on most machines is the 0.18.1 line, whose qbsp has no -q2bsp. Run the version probe afterwards.

capabilities.title: Compile a Quake II map into a BSP
capabilities.description: Reads .map source and writes the Quake II BSP, the portal file vis needs, the extended texinfo document light reads, and a point file when the map leaks.

capabilities.title: Compute the visible and hearable sets
capabilities.description: Quake II's vis computes a PHS — which clusters can be heard from which — as well as the PVS. That second pass has no Quake 1 equivalent.

capabilities.title: Compute lighting
capabilities.description: Writes the lightmap into the BSP. There is no .lit file: Quake II lightmaps are already coloured.

capabilities.title: Report what is inside a Quake II BSP
capabilities.description: bspinfo prints its report and, in the 2.x line, also writes a JSON dump, a geometry .obj and the lightmap atlases as PNG.

capabilities.title: Check a Quake II BSP for internal inconsistencies
capabilities.description: bsputil --check prints what it found and writes no file.

actions.title: Compile the map
actions.description: qbsp reads the .map and writes the Quake II .bsp. `-basedir` is the directory holding `textures/`, because qbsp has to open the .wal a face names to read the content and surface flags it bakes into the BSP; `-gamedir` is the mod that overlays it.

options.name: basename
options.title: Output name
options.description: The stem of the .bsp and of the files qbsp writes beside it.

options.name: format
options.title: BSP format
options.description: `Quake II` is the format every Quake II engine reads. `Qbism` is an extended format with higher limits, and was measured to write the ident QBSP:38 instead of IBSP:38 — an engine that has not been built for it will refuse the file.

options.name: leaktest
options.title: Fail if the map leaks
options.description: qbsp exits non-zero on a leak instead of writing a BSP with no visibility data. The point file and the leak portal file are still written, and are what you load in the editor to find the hole.

options.name: notex
options.title: Placeholder textures only
options.description: Writes no texture data into the BSP, for a build that depends on replacements or that must not carry anybody else's texture bytes.

options.name: subdivide
options.title: Texture subdivision
options.description: In luxels. qbsp's Quake II target sets 496 of its own accord; leave this unset to use it. 0 disables subdivision entirely.

options.name: maxedges
options.title: Maximum edges per face
options.description: How many edges a single face may have before qbsp splits it. Leave unset for the format's own limit.

options.name: filepriority
options.title: Search order
options.description: Whether loose files or packed archives are searched first when a texture is looked up.

diagnostics.message: A texture the map uses was not found under the base game data or the mod, so its contents and surface flags fall back to defaults.
diagnostics.hint: In Quake II the flags are read from the .wal itself, so a missing texture is a wrong BSP and not just a missing picture. Check what the base game data root is bound to. `skip` has no .wal and always reports this; that one line is expected.

diagnostics.hint: The palette lives in `pics/colormap.pcx` inside a copy of the game. Lighting colours will be approximate without it.

actions.title: Compute visibility and hearability
actions.description:
vis rewrites the BSP it is given. It also opens the .prt of the same stem in the same directory without being told to, which is why that file is an input here and is staged beside the BSP.

It writes a log, and this document does not declare it. Measured: 2.x writes `<stem>-vis.log` BESIDE THE BSP IT WAS GIVEN, not in the directory it was run in — a bsp at `inner/level.bsp` produces `inner/level-vis.log`. An input is staged into a directory of its own, so there is no path relative to the workspace that names it, and declaring one would declare an artifact that is never found. The job's captured output is the same text.

options.name: fast
options.title: Fast, rough visibility
options.description: A quick pass for previewing. The result is not what you ship.

options.name: level
options.title: Test level
options.description: vis's own 0-4. Ignored when the fast pass is on.

options.name: ambient_sounds
options.title: Ambient sounds
options.description: Quake II's vis also decides which ambient sounds a cluster hears — water, lava, sky. Turning this off writes none of them.

diagnostics.message: vis could not read the portal file that belongs to this BSP.
diagnostics.hint: The compile stage produces it. A leaked map has none, because qbsp stops before writing one.

diagnostics.message: The BSP has no visibility clusters, so there is nothing to compute.
The potentially hearable set was computed. Quake II uses it for sound; Quake 1 has no such pass.
Visibility data written.

roots.purpose: rewrite the staged BSP with its visibility and hearability data
read the Quake II palette the compilers load at startup
read the mod that overlays the base game data

actions.title: Compute lighting
actions.description: light rewrites the BSP it is given. Its log is not declared here for the same reason vis's is not: 2.x writes `<stem>-light.log` beside the BSP it was handed, which is inside the staged input's own directory. It also reads the `.texinfo.json` qbsp wrote beside that BSP — `Loading extended texinfo flags from …` — so that file is an input here and is staged with the BSP. Without it the run still succeeds, with the wrong surface flags, which is why it is wired rather than left to chance.

options.name: threads
options.title: Threads
options.description: More than one thread makes light faster and makes its output differ from run to run: measured on 2.0.0-alpha7, three runs of one map at four threads produced three different BSPs, and one thread produced the same one three times. Set it to 1 for a build whose BSP is byte-identical to the last one.

options.name: sampling
options.title: Supersampling
options.description: How many samples per lightmap texel. extra4 is the slow one you use for a final build.

options.name: gate
options.title: Light cutoff
options.description: Stop tracing a light below this brightness. Higher is faster and coarser; leave it unset for light's own default.

options.name: nolights
options.title: Ignore light entities
options.description: Only sunlight, minlight and emissive surfaces. Useful for checking what the textures themselves contribute.

actions.title: Report what is inside the BSP
actions.description: bspinfo prints its report — and, unlike the 0.18.1 build, also writes a JSON dump of the BSP, a geometry .obj and one PNG per lightmap atlas beside it. That is why this action asks to write to the workspace: a `read` root here would have been correct for Quake 1 and wrong for this.

options.name: basename
options.title: BSP name
options.description: The stem of the BSP being inspected. bspinfo names what it writes after the file it read, so this is how those artifacts are found: `<stem>.bsp.json` and `<stem>.bsp.geometry.obj`. The lightmap atlases it also writes are one PNG per atlas, a number nobody can declare in advance, so they are left in the workspace rather than claimed as outputs.
